title: Finite-sum nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax optimization with individually smooth components
summary: Unrestricted randomized component-gradient complexity is matched up to logarithmic factors under exact dual initialization and strong concavity only of the average.

description_paragraphs: Find first-order stationarity of the true reduced objective $\Phi(x)=\max_{y\in\mathbb R^{d_y}} f(x,y)$, where $f(x,y)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x,y)$, on unconstrained Euclidean spaces.
task.formulation: Find first-order stationarity of the true reduced objective $\Phi(x)=\max_{y\in\mathbb R^{d_y}} f(x,y)$, where $f(x,y)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x,y)$, on unconstrained Euclidean spaces.

description_paragraphs: Every component obeys the individual smoothness condition $\|\nabla f_i(z)-\nabla f_i(z^\prime)\|_2\le\beta\|z-z^\prime\|_2$ globally, with the same public beta.

Each component is continuously differentiable. Only the average dual function $f(x,\cdot)$ is required to be mu_y-strongly concave; individual components may be nonconcave in y. Thus the dual optimizer is unique and $\nabla\Phi(x)=\nabla_x f(x,y^\star(x))$.

The public initialization is $(0,0)$ with exact dual promise $y^\star(0)=0$ and primal gap $\Phi(0)-\inf\Phi\le\Delta$. The dimensions and n,beta,mu_y,Delta are public. Component gradients, query norms and dual optimizers away from the initial point need not be bounded.

description_paragraphs: At an adaptively selected index i and arbitrary joint point, receive only the exact full joint gradient $\nabla f_i(x,y)$. The same index always identifies the same fixed component. One component call costs one unit and a full mean gradient costs n. There are no function values, Hessians, reduced gradients or free dual maximizers in this interface.

The source lower bound is proved for the stronger packet $(f_i,\nabla f_i)$ and therefore applies to this gradient-only interface by discarding the extra value. The upper algorithms use only gradients.

description_paragraphs: Return any measurable primal point $\widehat x$, possibly unqueried and with unrestricted coordinate support. No dual point or certificate is required.

description_paragraphs: The error is $\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat x)\|_2$. The expected-squared criterion and constant-probability criterion are separate views with separate resource semantics.

description_paragraphs: Count every selected component joint-gradient call, including initialization and repetition. In the expected-RMS view optimize worst-instance expected work with almost sure termination. In the probability view require a fixed cap on every path. Internal arithmetic and memory are free. The matched quantities take a worst case over finite dimensions.

description_paragraphs: Queries, stopping decisions and outputs are arbitrary measurable functions of the observed history and public inputs. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed. Internal exact-real computation and storage are uncharged.
A private random seed independent of the fixed instance is permitted.
The instance is fixed before the private seed. Accuracy and expected work are each worst-case over individual instances.

regimes.name: IS / Expected RMS and work / small condition
regimes.predicate_text: $\beta,\Delta,\varepsilon>0$, $0<\mu_y\le\beta$, $a\ge a_{\rm U06}$, $n\ge1$, and $1\le\kappa\le\sqrt n$. Exact dual initialization is imposed. Upper algorithms apply to every finite pair of block dimensions. Lower bounds are worst cases over finite dimensions and can require exponential growth with the serialized path length, not merely polynomial dimension. In equation optimization-dimension the source block dimension is $D_0=\lceil32(8K_*+8)a_*^{-2}\sum_{t=0}^{H_0}n^t\rceil$, where $a_*=1/8600000$, $K_*=\lfloor c_{\rm inf}nH_0\rfloor$, $c_{\rm inf}=(a_*^2/2)^2/(4e)$, and $H_0=M_0m_0$ is the construction serial depth. The primal and dual blocks are assembled from this source as in Theorem distributional-hardness and Section parameter calibration. No fixed-dimensional or arithmetic-runtime matching conclusion follows.

objects.definition: Find first-order stationarity of the true reduced objective $\Phi(x)=\max_{y\in\mathbb R^{d_y}} f(x,y)$, where $f(x,y)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x,y)$, on unconstrained Euclidean spaces.
